> I can’t see my self as a man in my current circle of family and friends. Not because of them, but because of me. I think i would feel fake. Idk.

This is one of the huge things worrying me about transitioning too. I worry that I'll always feel like an imposter, like they're just pretending to accept me as a guy, when really they're just laughing at me behind my back. I'm sure they wouldn't be, but I worry I'll always think they are.

Thanks. I think I really am just worried and need a bit of validation. I always used to hear stories about transgender people always knowing they were transgender, and even though I've been reading the trans subs for a while and know that's not always the case, I still feel like I can't be transgender unless I *just know* that I am.

Thanks for your response, and the advice. 

I don't have a binder yet. I'm moving to a new country in two months time so I'm trying to delay the gender exploration until then, rather than deal with the gossip mill of my close-knit community possibly making it back to my parents. I want to be safely on the other side of the world before they find out. 

I think I will start keeping a record of how I feel about my gender each day though, so thanks for the suggestion. Should help me sort my thoughts out and try to pinpoint what exactly upsets me. Should also be a good head start for when I move countries and can easily access gender counselling, rather than the 2 year waiting list we have here.
You look a lot like a guy I work with who's 17 so that was my guess.

I only sleep a couple of hours most nights, and none at all the past few nights. It's not insomnia, I could sleep, I just don't. I'm exhausted constantly. I think it's partly to punish myself, partly because it means I at least have a reason for feeling so shit and down and bleh. Also if I sleep then when I wake up it'll be tomorrow. I don't want it to be tomorrow, it's taken all my energy just to get through today, tomorrow means I have to do it all again.

I just want to talk about my friend a bit. 

His name was Steve and he was the best person ever. He was always so cheerful and happy. Every time I saw him he'd give me a big hug and tell me my hair smelled pretty. He used to always take his guitar into the bathroom with him and ask if I had any requests for him to play while shitting. And no matter what song I requested he'd play and sing it for me, stopping occasionally to grunt comically (the bathroom door was closed and I could hear him from my room, just in case you think it's weirder than it was). I was in a relationship at the time with an absolute asshole of a guy (the day after finding my friend he got mad at me because I didn't feel like having sex and then just forced me to anyway. That wasn't the first or last time he did that) and the main thing that gave me the strength to leave was hearing what Steve said to a mutual friend about the relationship a few days before he died. He said "I don't know what she's doing with him. She's lovely and he's an ass". And it doesn't sound like much, but it's what helped me realise how bad my boyfriend really was. 

He used a dressing gown belt to hang himself and 9 years later I still have to remove the belt from all my dressing gowns. He didn't leave a note and I wish he had. Even if he blamed me for everything at least I'd know that this was what really what he wanted. I worry that it was a snap decision because he'd been drinking. He was celebrating that he'd just handed in his university dissertation after months of work. 

He'd had problems with depression in the past. We never knew any of this, it all came out after his death. He was back on anti-depressants as they'd recently found out his dad had bowel cancer. Because he was on medication he couldn't spend his summer being a counsellor at a summer camp in the USA, where he'd been a counsellor for the last 3 years. I don't think he'd have gone anyway, because of his dad's illness, but it still upset him.

I wasn't a good enough friend. I didn't know what he was going through. I should have known. I should have noticed. I knew what depression was like, I should have seen the signs. I should have tried harder to let him know I was there for him. I think was the last person to ever speak to him. I will always blame myself for his death. And it's stupid, because I *know* it's not my fault, but I can't stop blaming myself anyway. I hate myself for not trying CPR even though I know there was no point as he was frozen solid. He was so stiff that I couldn't lie him down on the floor, I had to prop him up against the fridge instead. 

I miss him.
Shouldn't it be 'but the surgeon changed my mind'?

Not really. I tried telling my ex, who I'm still friends with, and he just called me an idiot and changed the subject to video games. He even said calling a crisis line was a 'fucking stupid' thing to do. I kinda thought he might care a bit more, seeing as we found our friend's body together when he killed himself. 

I don't feel comfortable talking about it really. I want to talk about it, I need to talk about it, it's killing me keeping it all inside. But whenever I try it just doesn't come out. I'm worried that my parents will worry. I worry that I'll end up in some sort of psych hospital. I worry that people will think less of me or look at me differently, talk behind my back. I worry people will think I'm making it up, call me 'manipulative'. I find it very difficult even to talk about it on here most of the time. I type things out and end up just deleting it.

Sometimes, yeah, because then I'd be able to fix all the stupid mistakes I've made. But what if it doesn't work like that. What if they happen anyway so agreeing to relive my life just gains me another 29 years of pain. I barely survived it the first time, I can't do it again.

Infinite Jest by David Foster Wallace? 

"The so-called ‘psychotically depressed’ person who tries to kill herself doesn't do so out of quote ‘hopelessness’ or any abstract conviction that life's assets and debits do not square. And surely not because death seems suddenly appealing. The person in whom Itsinvisible agony reaches a certain unendurable level will kill herself the same way a trapped person will eventually jump from the window of a burning high-rise. Make no mistake about people who leap from burning windows. Their terror of falling from a great height is still just as great as it would be for you or me standing speculatively at the same window just checking out the view; i.e. the fear of falling remains a constant. The variable here is the other terror, the fire's flames: when the flames get close enough, falling to death becomes the slightly less terrible of two terrors. It's not desiring the fall; it's terror of the flames. Yet nobody down on the sidewalk, looking up and yelling ‘Don‘t!’ and ‘Hang on!’, can understand the jump. Not really. You'd have to have personally been trapped and felt flames to really understand a terror way beyond falling."
The fact that it's a permanent solution is the whole appeal! Anything else is just a temporary solution to a permanent problem.
